Assigning an array of tables over a dotted key captures the following dotted key

When a document contains a dotted key and I replace that key with an array of tables, the next dotted key in the document ends up rendered inside the new `[[...]]` section, so it silently changes meaning on the next parse.

Reproduction:

```python
import tomlkit

doc = tomlkit.parse("a.b = 1\nc.d = 2\n")
arr = tomlkit.aot()
tbl = tomlkit.table()
tbl["x"] = 9
arr.append(tbl)
doc["a"] = arr
print(repr(doc.as_string()))
print(tomlkit.parse(doc.as_string()))
```

Actual output: `'[[a]]\nx = 9\nc.d = 2\n'`. Because `c.d = 2` now follows the `[[a]]` header, re-parsing puts `c` inside the array entry instead of at the top level.

Expected output: the sibling stays at the top level, before the new header:

```
c.d = 2

[[a]]
x = 9
```

i.e. `doc.as_string() == "c.d = 2\n\n[[a]]\nx = 9\n"` and `tomlkit.parse(doc.as_string()) == {"c": {"d": 2}, "a": [{"x": 9}]}`. Replacing the dotted key with a regular table (`tomlkit.table()`) already behaves this way; arrays of tables should too, without changing the existing behavior for other replacements.
